Gaykhatu, on account of the ignoble traits that he possessed,
was overcome by dissolute desires,
and his mind wandered after every evil deed,
and his intellect strayed.
He was drawn to say to Baydu:
"I desire that your son be with me and in my service, and be a companion and associate to me."
The said Baydu, like a completely obedient and eager subject, assented to this,
and commanded that someone be sent in haste to bring his son.
Gaykhatu said:
"No,
but you yourself rise up and go in haste to your household before the news of the dispute that took place between me and you flies to them,
this dispute that has occurred between me and you,
lest those who belong to you be stirred up;
and as soon as you arrive,
send your son to come to me."
He, then, said:
"Let the king's command be done!"
And he went out from the camp like a bird from a snare,
looking behind him,
and journeying in one day the distance of every four days,
until he reached his home.
And he did not tarry at all,
but prepared and sent his son to Gaykhatu,
while he himself departed to the mountains of Hamadan, as if hunting.
And from there he sent an envoy to Ghazan, son of Arghun, weeping and lamenting,
and showed him everything that had happened to him,
while Gaykhatu perceived nothing,
but was immersed in hideous deeds {OCR?} and unmeasured extravagance.
And as an evil counterpart,
there presented himself before him the chief of the scribes {nomikoi}, that is, the Sahib-Diwan,
a certain Persian man whose name was Sadr al-Din.
And this man also was so {OCR?} prodigal,
that within a short space of time he emptied the treasuries of the kingdom of Gaykhatu.
And he began to borrow and spend,
until not even an apta {penny} remained to slaughter even a single sheep for the food of Gaykhatu himself.
Rather, a certain Jewish man was appointed,
whose name was Rashid al-Dawla,
to prepare food fitting for Gaykhatu,
of every kind that was needed,
wherever it was needed.
And so this Jew stood diligently in this business,
and spent a great sum from his own property,
and bought tens of thousands of sheep and cattle,
